items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: He had signed Dreams to Columbia Records and we did two semi-successful records for him.

ctx.x: Okay. I only heard a little thing. Well that was the general writing style, you know, my style at that point in time where we had had some success with one single that sold a lot called “Sneaking Up Behind You” on the first record, the first Brecker Brother record. Now I have to preface that, and I’ve told the story many times but I might as well recount it here. I had at one point in my life, and this was after joining Horace and I think it was — let me think for a second here — yeah it was after joining Horace…

friend Dave Sanborn who had just moved to New York or he was in Woodstock, he was close by. So that became an impetus for me to write — the cumulative effect of everything that had happened in my life, the music was the cumulative effect of everything that happened in my life both on the jazz side and on the jazz-rock or whatever you want to call it side. So I just got to work composing every day. And eventually we had rehearsals that a lot of the guys from the band Dreams — Will Lee on bass, Don Grolnick on…

jammed up a little [scats] I can’t even do it anymore, but a little horn line. And the next thing we know, we go in, Clive was in the studio. He loved it. The tune shot to number 2 on the R&B charts. And that’s what really sold The Brecker Brothers so to speak because they became really popular and this was in 19 — what year was it — 1975. “Sneaking Up Behind You” and that’s what sold the record and started our whole career. And we spent the last — I have to say, this is not great to say, but in a way we spent…
